headline: Hamburg jails two Iran agents who scouted Schuster and Beck; OpenAI says an ex-employee took 100+ files to Apple; Starlink backs down on illegal German price hikes; and AMD’s Verano Epyc jumps to 192 cores.

stories.title: Hamburg court jails two Iran agents who scouted Josef Schuster and Volker Beck
facts: Hanseatic Higher Regional Court: 8½ years (54) and 4½ years (43) for Iran intel work plus attempted murder/arson involvement — matching the federal prosecutor’s ask.

Judges found the Denmark-based pair had surveilled Zentralrat der Juden president Josef Schuster and DIG president Volker Beck; the older defendant also prepared a fire attack on a kosher grocery in Berlin.
Prosecutors say the older man took orders from Quds Force officers (IRGC foreign unit) and tried to recruit the younger man for an attack on Beck — or to find someone else to do it.
Defense had sought acquittals; Beck’s bid to join as a private accessory was earlier refused because no attack attempt had yet occurred.
stories.whyItMatters: A rare completed German trial tying IRGC tasking to concrete targeting of Jewish and pro-Israel figures on German soil — and it landed today, not as a tip.

stories.title: OpenAI alleges an ex-employee took 100+ confidential files to Apple
facts: In a San Jose federal filing, OpenAI says a staffer who left for Apple sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account, then presented the plans to senior Apple leadership months ago.
OpenAI ties the claim to Apple now shipping its own AI hardware (citing HomeView) and says it may countersue; a scheduled hearing in the existing trade-secrets fight was delayed.
Apple says it has hire-side procedures against using prior employers’ secrets and has found no evidence supporting the allegation.
This is separate from this week’s DOJ case against an OpenAI engineer charged with planting a recording device in an exec conference room.
stories.whyItMatters: The OpenAI–Apple trade-secrets war just got a new mirror allegation — and Apple’s HomeView launch is being used as Exhibit A for alleged reuse.

stories.title: Starlink signs a German cease-and-desist after illegal price hikes and forced upsells
facts: After a Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen warning, Starlink Internet Services Ltd gave an Unterlassungserklärung — it will stop the challenged practices rather than litigate.

In May 2026 Starlink raised Privathaushalt 200 Mbit/s from €49 to €55/month by email only (no active consent) and cut the advertised max speed; customers also reported silent switches into Privathaushalt Max at €75.
Affected customers can reclaim overpayments, VZ says — but on short month-to-month deals Starlink can still cancel and re-offer only at the new rate.
VZ contrasts Starlink’s climb-down with Amazon’s failed fight to the BGH over unilateral subscription hikes.
stories.whyItMatters: A concrete German consumer win against SpaceX’s ISP arm — and a reminder that EU contract law still bites satellite broadband.

stories.title: AMD’s Epyc 9006 LP “Verano” jumps to 192 Zen 6c cores for AI servers
facts: At OCP Global Summit 2026, Lisa Su previewed Epyc 9006 LP (codename Verano) — AMD’s LPDDR5x-on-package answer to Nvidia’s Vera — now with up to 192 cores vs earlier 72-core talk.
Design packs up to six 32-core Zen 6c chiplets, two LPDDR5x controllers on SOCAMM2 modules, and 128 MB L3 per CCD (vs 48 MB on Zen 6).
Aimed at AI workloads; pairs with Instinct GPUs over 112 Gbit/s XGMI. Ship window: H1 2027, with other Venice-9006 SKUs (Venice-X, Venice-HF) also slated for 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: AMD is putting a dense, memory-close CPU next to Nvidia’s rack story — and quietly tripling the core count vs last rumor.

facts.text: Peshawar: Al-Khair school roof collapse kills at least ~27–34 (mostly pupils) and injures 50+; owner detained, early read is structural failure.
Istanbul: two dead after the heaviest rainfall in 84 years, the governor said.
Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag (AfD+BSW, 44/83) urged a Ukraine course change — ceasefire, halt non-humanitarian aid/weapons, ease Russia sanctions; not binding on Berlin/EU.
BMI/BMDS/BSI published Germany’s PQC migration guideline: high-risk systems by end-2030, broad cutover largely by 2035.

facts.text: OpenAI Core Experimentation: GPT-6 Astra drove 1,400+ maintenance PRs (~800k LOC deleted); GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra hit ~92% of Astra’s stale-flag findings at ~14% API cost in one audit.

Vercel Sandbox $1M challenge: 1,285 reports, $242k paid, one Linux kernel networking 0-day (host mem leak / crash / code exec paths); no customer-data breach shown; Trail of Bits white-box + intern DM leak also fixed.
Junos OS: critical CVSSv3.1 9.8 vulns patched — official fix out (via Following).
